approach: Add a `fix: bool` field to `PlanEntry` (default false) and change the wave sort in `Plan::build_with` from `(e.rung, age)` to `(!e.fix, e.rung, age)`. Dependencies and the best-effective-priority filter run before that sort (plan.rs:769-783), so the key only orders ready items already in the same tier. Two places set the flag. (1) `reading::plan_entry` (topics.rs) flags a request whose text carries Hestia's root-cause anchor sentence (`terms::ROOT_CAUSE_ANCHOR`) or its `Gate under review: NAME.` line (`hestia::GATE_LINE`, made `pub(crate)`). Both anchors come from the generators `hestia::root_cause_request` and `hestia::gate_request`. (2) `RealSteps::entry_of` (drain.rs, the only production caller of `plan_entry`) ORs in a new pure function `steward_fix(records, job)`. It is true for a steward-channel job whose recorded work item is of kind BlindSpot or RepeatedFailure, linked the way `steward::decide` links an applied item: the job id is the last evidence reference, and the request was received at or after the item. Proposal-kind items (audience, website and study content, generic ideas) are never fixes. The rule is documented in the plan.rs module doc, the drain.rs module doc, the `athena drain` help and a new appended D183 entry. Tests: core unit tests for ordering, a cli unit test for classification, and drain integration tests for dispatch order, including one through the real `steward::decide` and `RealSteps` path.

decisions.choice: The fix key goes first in the wave sort: `(!e.fix, e.rung, age)`, so a fix precedes a feature even when the feature serves a higher rung.
decisions.reason: The request and acceptance criterion 5 say fix items come first inside a priority tier. Steward fixes are on the Implementation rung (`blind_spot_change`, steward.rs:759) and most owner-addendum features rank on a higher rung (`infer_rung`, topics.rs:254), so a key of (rung, !fix, age) would leave fixes starved, which is the complaint.

rejected.option: Key `(e.rung, !e.fix, age)`: fix before age only within a rung
rejected.why: A fix on the Implementation rung would still follow every higher-rung feature of the tier, so the starvation stays. This keeps the module doc's ladder order but does not meet the goal.

rejected.option: Raise fix requests one priority tier
rejected.why: Out of scope (priority levels and caps stay) and it would override `athena priority` and the tier caps.

decisions.choice: Carry the flag as a new `PlanEntry.fix` field, serialized only when true, like `on_hold` (plan.rs:177).
decisions.reason: `Plan::build_with` is pure over entries and has no records. Every `PlanEntry` literal outside `bare` already uses `..PlanEntry::bare(..)` (a search of `on_hold:` and `schema_problem:` finds only `bare` at plan.rs:287-288), so only `bare` changes and existing JSON is byte-identical.

rejected.option: Reuse `Improvement.items` (the id list of Steward and Hestia requests) as the fix set
rejected.why: Its documented meaning (plan.rs:477-479) is Athena's own requests for the guaranteed turn. It also holds spec-review and throughput-design requests, which are not fixes, and it omits gate-review requests (`improvement_of`, hestia.rs:973-1007).

rejected.option: Match titles such as `Fix the root cause`
rejected.why: `improvement_of` states requests are found by what the records link, never by title (hestia.rs:957-958).

decisions.choice: Hestia fixes are matched by the generated text anchors in `plan_entry`; steward fixes by the work item's kind in `entry_of`. `GATE_LINE` becomes `pub(crate)` (a visibility-only change in hestia.rs) so there is one definition.
decisions.reason: Neither a root-cause nor a gate-review job has a record link. `WorkItemKind` has only BlindSpot, RepeatedFailure and Proposal (work.rs:49-56). The root-cause request is found by its anchor sentence in terms.rs:50-53 and the gate request by its exact line (hestia.rs:1077-1084, 1140-1147).

rejected.option: Copy the gate line string into topics.rs
rejected.why: The two copies could drift. hestia.rs is not a listed deliverable, but a visibility keyword is the smaller risk than a silent mismatch.
That includes applied Proposals (website and study content, ideas) which the request says are not fixes.

decisions.choice: Link a steward-applied job to its work item by `evidence.last() == job` and `request.received_at >= work_item.at`.
decisions.reason: `steward::decide` pushes the queued job last onto the evidence of an applied item (steward.rs:705-713), and the request is stamped after the item's `now` (steward.rs:663-676). A RepeatedFailure item also cites failing jobs earlier in its evidence, so an `any` match would flag an unrelated open retry. A proposed-only item cites existing jobs, which were received before it, and the timestamp test excludes them.

rejected.option: Any evidence reference equal to the job
rejected.why: It would flag jobs a repeated-failure item merely cites.

risks.risk: A fix now precedes a higher-rung feature of the same priority tier, which reverses part of the documented ladder-first order for those items.
risks.mitigation: The request asks for fix-first inside a tier. D183 records the choice and the rejected `(rung, !fix, age)` key. Priority and dependencies still decide first, and a test pins that a fix never passes an urgent or high item.

risks.risk: Text matching: a hand-written request containing the root-cause anchor sentence or a `Gate under review:` line would count as a fix.
risks.mitigation: Both strings are generator-only shapes that the terms scan already treats as Athena's own text. A drift test builds the real root-cause request, and the gate line is one shared constant covered by the existing hestia test.

risks.risk: The steward link `evidence.last() == job` plus `received_at >= item.at` is a heuristic; a change to `steward::decide` would break it silently.
risks.mitigation: The criterion 4 real-steps test calls `decide` itself, so a change to the link fails a test. The timestamp guard keeps a proposed-only item that cites old jobs from flagging them.

risks.risk: Two files outside the listed deliverables are touched (a `pub(crate)` keyword in hestia.rs and help text in main.rs).
risks.mitigation: Both are one-line, behavior-free edits that remove a duplicated string and a stale statement; the plan names them so the producer and verifier see them.

risks.risk: A steward Proposal that is really a bug fix (a generic idea about a failure) is not flagged, because the kind rule limits fixes to blind-spot and repeated-failure items.
risks.mitigation: This follows the request's definition (root-cause, repeated-failure, blind-spot, gate-review). Out of scope: changing how the steward classifies items. D183 lists it as a limit.

demonstrations.method: A unit test in the `plan.rs` test module, `a_fix_entry_is_ordered_before_an_older_feature_entry_of_its_tier`. It builds two normal-priority entries with the existing `entry()` helper (plan.rs:1159): `feature` first (older) and `fixer` second with `fix = true`, same rung, disjoint paths. It asserts `Plan::build(&entries).order == ["fixer", "feature"]`, and also that with `fix = false` the order is `["feature", "fixer"]` (the age tiebreak). A second pair differs in rung: the fix is on the Implementation rung and the feature on Brief requirements. The fix still comes first, which pins the key as `(!fix, rung, age)`. The same `cargo test -p athena-core` run also runs the `refusal_corpus` target; the new text match refuses nothing, and the cases (`root-cause-cites-two-jobs-without-relying`, the generated root-cause cases) must still pass.
demonstrations.observes: The order puts the fix entry first; with the flag false the order is by age.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the `!e.fix` term in the sort key at plan.rs:783 the order is `[feature, fixer]` and the assertion fails.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry point `Plan::build` -> `Plan::build_with` (plan.rs:668, 692). Fixture: `PlanEntry` values built by the existing `entry()` test helper, with `fix` set by a field update (`..` syntax). No double. The `fix` field is added by plan step 1.

demonstrations.method: Two unit tests in plan.rs tests. (a) `a_fix_flag_never_overrides_priority`: an older urgent feature, a high feature and a normal fix, all ready. The order is urgent, high, fix. A low-priority fix still follows a normal feature. `plan.priority_violations(&entries)` (plan.rs:1823-1843 shows its use) is empty. (b) `a_fix_flag_never_overrides_dependencies`: a normal `fixer` with `fix = true` that lists `base` (a non-fix feature) in `depends_on`, plus an unrelated non-fix older item. `base` precedes `fixer`; and a normal fix that is a prerequisite of a high feature takes the effective high priority and still comes first. `Plan::build_capped` over a fix and non-fix urgent group (`CAPS`, plan.rs:1667) keeps its tier counts and the person-set entry first.
demonstrations.observes: An urgent or high feature stays ahead of a normal fix, and a dependent stays behind what it needs, with the flag set.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the fix key were placed before the priority filter or before dependency readiness, the normal fix would precede the urgent feature, or the dependent would precede its base. Both assertions fail.

demonstrations.method: A unit test in the `drain.rs` test module (it is `use super::*`, drain.rs:4951-4952). The pure function `steward_fix(&Records, &JobRecords) -> bool` (added in step 4) is called with a `Records::default()` that the test fills. It holds a steward-channel request job for website or study content, and a `WorkItem` of kind Proposal (role `audience` or `steward`, the same shape as `audience::work_item`, audience.rs:98-116) whose last evidence is that job. The result is false. The test then builds `Plan::build_with` from an older normal feature entry and the content entry carrying that flag. The older item is first, so the content request keeps its age place. Contrast arms: the same job with kind BlindSpot and with kind RepeatedFailure is true. A BlindSpot item whose last evidence is a different job, or whose `at` is later than the request's `received_at`, leaves the job false. A request without the steward channel is false. A plain content request text gives `plan_entry(..).fix == false`.
demonstrations.observes: A content request is not flagged and stays in age order behind older items of its tier; the fix kinds are flagged, so the detector is not constantly false.
demonstrations.fails_without: A detector that flagged every steward-channel request, or looked only at role or title, would mark the Proposal-kind content job as a fix and the first assertion fails.
demonstrations.seam: `steward_fix` is added to drain.rs by step 4 and is called from `RealSteps::entry_of` (drain.rs:4339). It is pure over in-memory `Records` (public `jobs`, `work_items` fields; `Records::default()` is used the same way in status.rs tests) and `JobRecords`/`Request`. No double; `athena_core::reading::plan_entry` is the real function.
